Definition: Laish, the name of two places in Palestine
BiblicalUsage: Laish the place is a different word from layish the lion, though they share the same letters — this one is a town, and a man's name, in the north. In Judges 18:7, "and came to Laish"; and in Judges 18:27, "and came unto Laish". In 1 Samuel 25:44, "to Phalti the son of Laish".
TheologicalSignificance: I believe Laish shows both sides of a name — a careless city taken by Dan, and a father whose son lost his wife to a king. I hold that names in Scripture carry whole histories, and God remembers every one of them.
